title: Attention kernel harmonizer: dynamic stride selection and memory-safe staging
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Since integrating FlashAttention v3, several workloads (long-context chat and batched prefill-heavy workloads) have seen intermittent OOMs and startup latency spikes during prefill. Root causes appear to be a combination of v3's larger workspace requirements for certain stride/tiling shapes and our historical kernel selection heuristics that do not consider dynamic token distribution across heads or staging memory for large-prefill requests.

Goal: Build an "Attention kernel harmonizer" layer in the runtime kernel selection path that: (1) dynamically selects per-request stride/tiling parameters for v3 vs v2 variants based on a quick lightweight fingerprint of the request (sequence len distribution, head count, dtype/quantization), (2) stages prefill memory allocation in small commits to avoid large instantaneous workspace spikes, and (3) implements a safety net to fall back to v2/quantized kernels when estimated workspace exceeds safe thresholds.

Deliverables: a) harmonizer selection algorithm and heuristics, b) memory staging shim and micro-commit allocator for prefill, c) integration tests, e2e perf/oom benchmarks, d) canary rollout plan and dashboards for detection and rollback, e) PRs with feature flag gating and telemetry.

Success metrics: reduce prefill-related OOM rate by >= 90% on canary customers, eliminate median prefill startup 95th percentile latency spike (target < 150ms additional), and keep token throughput change < 5% on p90 latency compared to baseline for most workloads.

Notes: this is explicitly a runtime-side mitigation to avoid wholesale disabling of FlashAttention v3 for affected customers; long-term we should feed findings to the FlashAttention upstream team and to our compilation/kernel autotuner.
comments: 2026-03-01 — Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after reproducing deterministic OOM on internal repro harness: 16x40B model, batch=8, prefill=4096 tokens, dtype=float16 produced workspace spike > 20GB on RTX A100 which triggered OOM. Attached minimal repro script to GH issue.

2026-03-03 — Jonah Li: Initial profiling with nvprof and custom malloc hooks shows that FA3 kernel variants allocate ephemeral workspace that scales with head-block stride; some stride shapes in our selector are optimistic and map to high-workspace kernel paths. Early idea: compute a cheap 'workspace estimate' function from (seq_len, batch, head_size, num_heads, dtype, quant_mode) and use that to veto v3 selection when estimate > threshold.

2026-03-05 — Jonah Li: POC: added estimate shim to kernel-scorer. Running the nightly prefill benchmark shows OOMs drop to 5% but 95th-percentile latency jumps by 12% due to forced fallback to v2 in many cases. Logged perf numbers: baseline p95 prefill latency 420ms -> POC 470ms; p99 OOMs decreased from 8.7% to 0.8% on the repro fleet. Links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1289 (draft).

2026-03-07 — Lina Park (SRE): Observability plan proposed: add prefill_workspace_estimate metric and kernel_choice tag to per-request traces, and create alert when average workspace_estimate > 0.8 * node_gpu_mem. Dashboard template PR: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/abcd-prefill-ooms.

2026-03-09 — Jonah Li: Implemented memory-safe staging prototype: allocator that commits workspace in micro-commits (512MB chunks) and runs a pre-check for cumulative allocation vs soft limit; this prevents single-shot large allocations and gives opportunity to degrade to streaming attention or v2 when stage fails. Benchmarks: micro-commit reduces peak allocation spikes by ~30% in the repro case and keeps v3 path alive in 60% of cases that previously would fall back. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1298

2026-03-10 — PM review (Ravi Desai): Concern about end-to-end latency; asked for canary test plan and gating flags. Created canary checklist with abort thresholds and owner rotations. Added label 'customer-facing' to trial customers.

2026-03-11 — Design (Marina Ortega): UX note for Console: would like kernel_choice and workspace_estimate exposed as per-route telemetry and in the rollouts UI for the canary so PM/SE teams can opt into more aggressive v3 selection or pin to v2. Filing follow-up ticket in product-management.

2026-03-12 — Jonah Li: Prepared rollout plan: 1) internal canary on staging nodes (runtime-1.22-canary, feature flag runtime.attn_harmonizer=true), 2) 5% production traffic for low-risk customers, 3) ramp to 30% with automated rollback if OOMs or p95 latency > 10% uplift, 4) full rollout. Added e2e benchmark artifacts: https://storage.redwood.ai/benchmarks/attn_harmonizer/2026-03-12/results.html. Next: finalize autotuner integration to refine stride scoring (blocked by dependency ENG-118901 autotuner metrics export).
acceptance_criteria: Automated unit/integration tests validating harmonizer chooses v3 when estimate within threshold and falls back when above
e2e benchmark reproducible with our harness showing OOM reduction >= 90% on repro fleets
Canary rollout plan documented and validated (abort thresholds, owners, dashboards)
PR merged with feature flag and default-off for now
